content.text:
`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

`cmd/entire/cli/dispatch_wizard_scope.go:99-115`

<result>Read the diff, the huh v2.0.3 source, and the surrounding CLI infrastructure. Six altitude findings.

## Findings

**1. `ensureScope` in `WithHideFunc` — the form is being used as a scheduler, and huh's model doesn't support it**
`/Users/alisha/.marvin/worktrees/cli/cli-dispatch-jurisdiction/cmd/entire/cli/dispatch_wizard.go:282-291, 317-321, 339-345`
Hide funcs are not "the form goroutine" in the benign sense the comment assumes. `Form.isGroupHidden` is called from `UpdateFieldPositions`, which runs (a) synchronously inside `huh.NewForm` (`form.go:127`, reached via `uiform.New`) and (b) on **every `tea.KeyPressMsg` inside `Form.Update`** (`form.go:628`), plus at `form.go:519/592/611`. So the blocking `loadScope()` join lands on the bubbletea event loop the first keypress after the user picks Cloud: up to `dispatchWizardScopeTimeout` (10s) plus an unbounded gateway repo-list call with the UI frozen, no spinner, and no Ctrl-C. The background `go loadScope()` only helps if the user dawdles on Mode — the "rarely waits" premise isn't guaranteed by anything. Secondarily, the comment's own safety argument doesn't hold: `state.jurisdiction`/`state.scope` are written here (event loop) and read by `loadRepos` from a `tea.Cmd` goroutine (`field_multiselect.go:338`) with no synchronization.
*Deeper fix:* let huh own the async. Drop `ensureScope` entirely and put the wait inside the jurisdiction `OptionsFunc` — that already runs on a `tea.Cmd` goroutine under huh's own loading spinner (`field_select.go:364-372`) — returning options in default-first order so `Select` seeds `state.jurisdiction` from option[0] via huh's normal binding instead of a manual write. `hasPicker` then becomes a read of a value cached by that same `sync.OnceValue`, so the hide func stays a pure predicate. The alternative — resolve the scope before `NewAccessibleForm` behind the spinner in `dispatch_tui.go` — is simpler but makes Local-mode users pay for cloud calls.
*Cost:* ~40 lines in `runDispatchWizard`, one new test driving the form; roughly half a day. Requires accepting that the jurisdiction default is expressed as option ordering rather than an assignment.

**2. Fourth hand-rolled "read the whole repo index" call site**
`dispatch_wizard_scope.go:141-166` (and the constant at `:15-18`)
`newCellCoreClient()` + `ListRepos(ctx, ListReposParams{})` + a 10s timeout + an `index.Truncated` warning is already written out at `search_cmd.go:525-543`, in `search_v4.go`'s `listFullIndex`, and in `repo_mirror.go:866/910`. The comment even says the timeout is "the same budget code search gives the same call" — the constant was copied rather than shared.
*Deeper fix:* one `listRepoIndex(ctx)` helper beside `cell_fanout.go`, which already owns the index→routing vocabulary, owning client construction, the timeout constant, and the truncation warning; the wizard keeps only the entries→jurisdictions mapping.
*Cost:* ~20 lines moved, but it touches both search paths, so their tests must be re-run. Small.

**3. "repo → ready jurisdictions" is now built two different ways**
`dispatch_wizard_scope.go:141-166` vs `dispatch_jurisdiction.go:66-88`
Reusing `readyPlacementJurisdictions` is the right call and I'd keep it. But the map around it is now duplicated: the hint builds it per-repo via `lookupRepoIndexEntry` on a 3s-per-repo budget keyed by the user's typed slug; the wizard builds it from one full index read on 10s keyed by lowercased slug. Two shapes, two budgets, two key conventions for the same question.
*Deeper fix:* one `repoReadyJurisdictions(ctx, client, repos ...string)` in `dispatch_jurisdiction.go` (empty variadic = full index), returning a lowercase-keyed map; both callers use it.
*Cost:* ~40 lines consolidated. The real work is reconciling the two timeout policies (garnish-on-an-error vs blocking-a-picker) — they may legitimately differ, in which case pass the budget in.

**4. `auth.HomeJurisdiction` is at the right layer but claims authority it doesn't have**
`/Users/alisha/.marvin/worktrees/cli/cli-dispatch-jurisdiction/cmd/entire/cli/auth/cell_data_api.go:578-592`
The layer is defensible: `resolveJurisdiction` (`:381-397`) routes on the `home_jurisdiction` claim, so for "where would we route by default" the claim *is* the operative value, and `resolveCellSubject` is unexported so the wizard can't compose this itself. The altitude problem is the name and doc: `auth.go:441-448` establishes that `/me`'s `global.homeJurisdiction` is *authoritative* for the home jurisdiction with the claim as fallback. There are now two exported-ish answers to "what is my home jurisdiction" that can silently disagree (stale claim after a home migration) with nothing linking them.
*Deeper fix:* name it for what it is — `RoutingHomeJurisdiction`, or `HomeJurisdictionFromActiveLogin` — and say in the doc that the profile answer is `/me`'s. Or, more thoroughly, have `auth` expose the single `/me`-preferred resolver and let `runAuthStatus` call it, keeping the claim-only path as the explicitly-named routing variant.
*Cost:* rename is trivial (one call site). Unifying is medium and drags a `/me` round-trip into a path that deliberately avoids one.

**5. `showRepoPicker()` is now production-dead**
`dispatch_wizard.go:132-134`
The repo group's hide func was rewritten to `state.isLocal()` inline (to hang the `ensureScope()` side effect off it), leaving `showRepoPicker` referenced only by `dispatch_wizard_test.go:121/126`. The state predicate that used to express "which groups show" was bypassed rather than extended.
*Deeper fix:* delete it and its two test assertions (it falls out naturally once finding 1 restores pure predicates).
*Cost:* trivial.

**6. `resolveCloudRepos` is a third enforcement point for "one dispatch, one jurisdiction"**
`dispatch_wizard.go:107-130`
The invariant is now enforced in three places: the restricted option list, huh's own narrowing (`updateOptionsMsg` → `selectOptions` → `updateValue` rewrites `state.selectedRepos` to the intersection with the new option set, `field_multiselect.go:362-370`), and this filter. None of them is `dispatch/options.go`, which owns `Options` and whose consumer — the cell — is what actually 404s on a cross-jurisdiction repo. A wizard state accessor silently discarding a user's selection is the wrong home for a domain rule (mitigated: the confirm summary shows the surviving list).
*Deeper fix:* if the rule is real, validate it in `resolveDispatchOptions` so `--repos` + `--jurisdiction` gets the same treatment as the wizard; the wizard's filter then becomes redundant with huh's narrowing and can go.
*Cost:* low-medium — needs a decision on whether the flag path should hard-error instead of silently dropping (I'd expect error there, drop here).

## Explicit non-findings

- **Two catalogues is not avoidable.** `api.Repository` (`api/repositories.go:11-14`) carries only `full_name` + `checkpoint_count`; `coreapi.RepoIndexEntry` carries `Placements` but no checkpoint count. No single source answers "offerable and placed where". Only the join's *location* is debatable, and findings 2-3 cover that.
- **"READY placements only" is right and consistent.** It reuses `readyPlacementJurisdictions`, so the wizard offers exactly the slugs the placement hint offers and the `--jurisdiction` flag accepts. Its divergence from `routedRepoPlacement` (one elected processing primary, ready) is correct, not an inconsistency: that rule exists to dedup mirrors for *search indexing*, whereas the hint's existence proves a cell answers dispatch for any ready placement. Worth a one-line comment in `dispatch_wizard_scope.go` pointing at `routedRepoPlacement` to say the difference is deliberate.
- **`insecureHTTP: false` hardcoded** in `defaultResolveDispatchWizardHome` matches the wizard's existing stance (`state.resolve()` already passes `false` for `InsecureHTTPAuth`), so it's pre-existing, not introduced here.</result>

content.text:
`/simplify` done — committed as `4d7f702ac` (five commits on the branch, nothing pushed).

## What was fixed

**The big one (efficiency + altitude agreed):** the picker loaded its catalogue from a group hide func. huh evaluates those on the Bubble Tea event loop on every keypress, so the first step into cloud mode froze the form — no spinner, no Ctrl-C — until three network calls returned; the default it wrote into form state also raced with the repo picker's options goroutine; and the eager background load ran for local-mode users who never need it. Now the Jurisdiction select's `OptionsFunc` does the loading (huh runs it off the event loop under its own spinner, only in cloud mode) and the default is expressed as option order, which huh binds into the state itself. Hide funcs are pure predicates again.

**Smaller:**
- Scope is precomputed once (jurisdiction → repos map, sorted keys, default) instead of five overlapping catalogue scans per render; `slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(...))` replaces the hand-rolled set→sort.
- Dropped the redundant selection filter and `state.scope` — huh already narrows the bound selection when options change (two reviewers verified against huh's source).
- `showRepoPicker` is live again instead of inlined; `loadRepos` misnomer gone.
- `auth.HomeJurisdiction` → `HomeJurisdictionFromActiveLogin`, documented as the routing claim, not the authoritative `/me` home.
- Tests collapsed into one table; unused stub parameter removed. Net −46 lines.

**Skipped (noted):**
- A shared `listRepoIndex` helper for the four call sites that read the whole control-plane index (search ×2, mirror, wizard) — worthwhile, but touches the search paths; separate change.
- Merging the hint's per-repo lookup with the wizard's full-index map — different budgets/keying are deliberate.
- Deriving home from the token the placements client already minted (saves one refresh) — the client interface doesn't expose it; small win, not worth widening the seam now.

Verification: lint 0 issues; 10,035 unit tests pass; wizard tests green under `-race`.

Every `NewRefreshingLoginProvider` constructs a fresh `tokenmanager.Manager` (`auth/refresh.go:124`), and `Manager.Refresh` reads the store on *every* call, even the fast path (`tokenmanager.go:945-958` `ensureFreshLogin` → `loadTokenSet`), where `contextTokenStore.LoadTokens` does two `tokenstore.Get` keyring calls (`auth/refresh.go:41,55`). `contexts.Load` has no memoization either (`contexts.go:73-83`, file-locked read each time). Only the *exchanged* token cache is in-process, and it is per-Manager (`m.cache`), so it never helps here.

**Expired-JWT contention is serialized but harmless.** The three Managers share one cross-process lock path (`processLock()` keyed on ClientID+Issuer, `tokenmanager.go:765-767`), and `freshOrProceed` re-reads the store after each gate (`:996-1005`), so late waiters reuse the first grant rather than burning three rotations. Redundant, not incorrect.

**Simpler path exists.** Goroutine 3 adds nothing goroutine 2 doesn't already hold: `auth.ResolveControlPlaneTarget()` returns `TokenSource` yielding the bare login JWT (`control_plane.go:33-35,102`), and `auth.HomeJurisdictionFromLoginJWT` (`cell_data_api.go:600`) reads the claim from it, so the placements goroutine could derive `home` from the same token (mind the `ENTIRE_TOKEN` bypass, which `coreapi.New` and `resolveCellSubject` both honour but `ResolveControlPlaneTarget` does not — the merged path must keep that parity). Note the `coreapi.Client` itself exposes no token accessor (only `CoreOrigin`, `client.go:135`), so the fix is at the target level, not the client.

**Nuance:** goroutine 1 predates this PR (`dispatch_wizard.go:26` exists at HEAD; diff line 1438 shows the old call), so the PR adds two new resolutions, not three; and because all three run concurrently, wall-clock cost is roughly the slowest keyring read, not the sum.
